title: a comment devbin ships is shaped like a home directory path, and a consumer's guard refuses that estate's own tracked copy
body:
## What happens

`lib/helpers:1517` carries the text `~/Users/...` inside a comment. It is prose: the comment explains what an empty `HOME` would make the writer record, and the string is the example of the wrong value rather than a path anything resolves.

Cdtempl's ST0005 AT-00.6 arm (`test/cdtempl.bats:1149`) refuses any tracked file matching `/Users/[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+|/home/[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`. A dot sits inside that character class, so `~/Users/...` matches on its `/Users/...` half. Cdtempl vendors the file at `bin/.devbin/lib/helpers`, where it is the same line 1517, so Cdtempl's own guard refuses Cdtempl's own tracked copy of devbin's bytes.

Measured here: that pattern has exactly one hit across the whole vendored seam, and it is this line. `git blame` gives `187219e`, which is 0069's own fix, and `git tag --contains 187219e` answers v0.1.1 through v0.1.5, so every estate at 0.1.1 or later carries it. Reported by vc, who also read Cdtempl's CI: red on this since the 2026-09-18 push (run 35374380997, test 108, on both runners), and Cdtempl is public. That run is vc's reading and not mine.

## Why this is devbin's to fix and not Cdtempl's

The guard is working. A consumer cannot tell devbin's prose from a real path, and a pattern that could would have to understand English. Devbin ships these bytes into every estate that vendors it, so devbin owns the constraint. No behaviour moves: the comment is the whole defect and the whole fix.

## Fix

Reword the comment in `lib/helpers` so it carries nothing shaped like a home path, `/home/<name>` included, since the same guard covers both. Say in place why the example is described rather than shown, so the next author does not put the shape back.

Add an arm that runs the consumer's predicate over devbin's own vendored seam, so the next instance is caught here instead of in a public estate's CI.

**The arm's scope is the SEAM, never the repository.** Measured at HEAD: 31 tracked files match that pattern. Twenty-nine are records -- archived boards under `intent/whiteboard/*/.history/`, canon issue JSON, `intent/wip.md` -- and one is `tests/unit/install.bats`, whose 0069 fixtures are home paths on purpose. Scrubbing the operator's home path out of history is parked by hv (2026-09-16) on the condition that devbin writes no home path into any TRACKED file, so a repository-wide arm would go red on the parked records and force that ruling by accident. What reaches an estate is what `vendored_paths` enumerates, and that is the population this defect lives in.

## Tests

`tests/unit/install.bats`, in a section of its own beside the 0069 arms it belongs with. Every path `vendored_paths` names, resolved to its source through `vendor_source_path`, is refused if it matches the guard's pattern.

The arm carries two controls. A positive control, because a scan whose pattern has stopped matching reports the same clean as a seam that is clean: a file holding a home path must be caught by the same probe, in the same run. And a population floor, because a `vendored_paths` that answered nothing, or nearly nothing, would make the scan vacuous and green.

Red first: the arm names `lib/helpers` before the comment is reworded, and the positive control is then broken deliberately to prove it can fail.

## Resolution

Fixed at `7de940d`, the new arm driven red first against the offending line.

The comment in `lib/helpers` describes the example rather than writing it out, and records in place why, citing this issue so the shape does not return. `tests/unit/install.bats` gains a scan that runs the consumer's own predicate over `vendored_paths`, resolving each path through `vendor_source_path`, so the enumeration is devbin's single one rather than a second list.

The arm carries three controls, because the failure modes here are all silent: a population floor, so a broken enumeration fails rather than reporting the clean of an empty scan; a probe control exercising BOTH halves of the alternation, `/Users/` and `/home/`, after `critic-shell` found the first version drove only one; and a status branch that tells "could not read this file" from "this file is clean", where the first version collapsed them.

Verified independently by vc on the committed tree: 45 files across `lib/` and `bin/devbin`, zero matches for the consumer's pattern, probe control hitting; and `git grep -lIE` over the same paths returns nothing. The pre-fix bytes do match at `lib/helpers:1517`, so the arm has a real red state and it is the right one.

Reach, measured: the line entered at `187219e`, the fix for issue 0069, and `git tag --contains` puts it in v0.1.1 through v0.1.5. Every estate on 0.1.3 vendors a copy. Only Cdtempl's guard catches it, and Cdtempl's CI has been red on it since its 2026-09-18 push (run 35374380997, test 108, on both runners). It clears there when 0.1.6 is swept in.

Full suite 1600/1600 at `993c995` (this commit's child), 0 not ok. Ships in 0.1.6.
